evals.query: I've redesigned parts of the issue list in our bug tracker. My lead has to approve before anything ships. Last time they approved 'the redesign' in a meeting and then objected to half of it after launch. The current screen and my list of changes are attached. Prepare what I should send my lead.
expected_behavior: Gives one item per change so each can be approved or rejected on its own, and splits change 4 (moving the button and renaming it) into two.
Shows today and the proposal side by side for each item (images, rendered HTML, or precise before and after of the same area).
Asks for an explicit answer per item (for example approve, reject, discuss) and records it, so a blanket approval is not possible.
Flags risks the lead should weigh on specific items (for example priority shown by colour alone, the date only on hover not working on tablets).
Makes clear that only approved items will ship.
Is quick to answer in one sitting: a scannable page or table, not a long memo.

evals.query: Every design review for our app's new onboarding goes in circles: eight people comment on everything at once and we leave without decisions. Next week I present the redesign again. How should I run it so we actually leave with decisions?
expected_behavior: Breaks the redesign into separate, specific decisions instead of presenting it as one whole.
Shows the current and proposed version of each change next to each other.
Frames a specific question per item with set answers (for example approve, reject, needs work) and records each answer.
Says who decides, or the decision rule, so eight opinions don't block a decision.
Uses the time before and after the meeting (for example a pre-read with a response per item, and a written record of decisions sent afterwards).
Gives the plan as a short sequence of steps.
